title: The profiled component Fisher price controls every admissible amplitude

fisher_floor.shell: Use b_N=(ceil(N/4),ceil(N/4),ceil(N/4)), N/16<=ell_N<=N/8 and d_N=ell_N^3; then omega_k/N>=sqrt(3)/4 and d_N/N^3<=1/512.
fisher_floor.exact_term: With r_(N,k)=sqrt(omega_k^2+kappa_N)/N and t_(N,k)=eta r_(N,k) in (0,1), C_(F,N)=(N/2)sum eta r_(N,k)^2/[1-eta r_(N,k)].
fisher_floor.amplitude_inequality: The identity (2t-1)^2>=0 gives t/(1-t)>=4t^2 and hence C_(F,N)>=2N eta^2 sum r_(N,k)^3 for every admissible amplitude.
fisher_floor.profile_self_consistency: For kappa_g=24gD(kappa_g), rationalization on [-1,1]^3 gives D(kappa)>=4kappa/[sqrt(3)sqrt(3+kappa)(sqrt(3)+sqrt(3+kappa))], so g>=8sqrt(3) implies kappa_g>=16sqrt(3)g-3>=g.
fisher_floor.large_coupling: K1572 convergence kappa_N/N^2->kappa_g gives C_(F,N)/N^4>=2eta^2(d_N/N^3)(g/2)^(3/2) for all sufficiently large N.
fisher_floor.scope_guard: The theorem uses the exact K1572 profile, the explicit shell and positive residual covariance; it is not an unrestricted Fisher inequality.
